== History ==
[[File:Kurogane-mochi at Suhama Shrine.jpg|Thumbnail|The {{ill|Ilex rotunda|arz|اليكس روتوندا|ceb|Ilex rotunda|es|Ilex rotunda|et|Ümar iileks|fa|خاس کوروگانه|id|Ilex rotunda|ja|クロガネモチ|ko|먼나무|sv|Ilex rotunda|uk|Ilex rotunda|vi|Ilex rotunda|war|Ilex rotunda|zh|鐵冬青|zh_yue|鐵冬青|qid=Q844306}} tree (a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=protected tree}}) within the shrine grounds]]
According to tradition, the shrine was once considered identical in essence to {{ill|Izumo-taisha|abstract|Q696362|ar|إزومو-تايشا|cs|Svatyně Izumo|de|Izumo-Taisha|es|Izumo Taisha|eu|Izumo-taisha|fi|Izumo-taisha|fr|Izumo-taisha|gl|Izumo Taisha|he|איזומו טאיישה|hu|Izumo-taisa|id|Izumo Taisha|it|Santuario di Izumo|ja|出雲大社|jv|Izumo Taisha|ka|იძუმო-ტაიშა|ko|이즈모 대사|la|Izumo-taisha|mk|Изумо-тајша|or|ଇଜୁମୋ ତାଇଶା|pl|Izumo-taisha|pt|Santuário de Izumo|ro|Marele Sanctuar de la Izumo|ru|Идзумо тайся|simple|Izumo-taisha|th|ศาลเจ้าอิซูโมะ|tr|Izumo-taisha|uk|Святилище Ідзумо|wuu|出云大社|zh|出雲大社|qid=Q696362}} and held its grand festival on October 7. Although the details of its founding are unclear, it is already listed in the Heian-period “{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932}},” and it is the only {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} within Daitō City. From {{ill|Sasara district|ja|讃良郡|zh|讚良郡|qid=Q11632569}} to {{ill|Wakae district|ja|若江郡|zh|若江郡|qid=Q11616589}}, it once had parishioners from several dozen villages. In 1873 (Meiji 6), it became the {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}} for eleven villages within Sanra District, and in September 1907 (Meiji 40), three shrines—{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ōtani Shrine}} in Teragawa, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ryūma Shrine}} in Ryūma, and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Zama Shrine}} in Fukano—were temporarily merged into it. Today, it serves as the {{ill|Ubusunagami|ja|産土神|ko|산토신|zh|產土神|qid=Q1392097}} (local tutelary deity) of Nakagaito.

;About the shrine name
In ancient times, the area where this shrine stands was part of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kawachi Bay}}, which later became {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kawachi Lagoon}}, then {{ill|Kawachi Bay|ja|河内湖|qid=Q11553429}}, gradually shrinking due to sediment inflow from rivers such as the {{ill|Yodo River|ar|نهر يودو|arz|نهر يودو|ceb|Yodo-gawa (suba sa Hapon, lat 34,68, long 135,42)|de|Yodo (Fluss)|es|Río Yodo|eu|Yodo ibaia|fa|رود یودو|fi|Yodojoki|fr|Yodo-gawa|id|Sungai Yodo|it|Yodo|ja|淀川|ko|요도가와강|ms|Sungai Yodo|nl|Yodo|no|Yodo (elv)|pl|Yodo|pt|Rio Yodo|ru|Йодо|sl|Jodo (reka)|th|แม่น้ำโยโดะ|tr|Yodo Nehri|zh|淀川|qid=Q1140505}} and the {{ill|Yamato River|arz|نهر ياماتو|ceb|Yamato Gawa|es|Río Yamato|fa|رود یاماتو|fr|Yamato-gawa|gl|Río Yamato|it|Yamato (fiume)|ja|大和川|ko|야마토강|my|ယမတိုမြစ်|ru|Ямато (река)|zh|大和川|qid=Q9001527}}. As this happened, settlements were gradually established, though large ponds such as {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Fukakai Pond}} and {{ill|Fukano Pond|qid=Q11560330}} remained. It is said that the western side of this shrine once bordered such waters, and there is a theory that the shrine originally enshrined not {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ca|Ōkuninushi|es|Ōkuninushi|fa|اوکونینوشی|fr|Ōkuninushi|hu|Ókuninusi|id|Ookuninushi|it|Ōkuninushi|ja|大国主|ko|오오쿠니누시|mni|ꯑꯣꯀꯨꯅꯤꯅꯨꯁꯤ|pl|Ōkuninushi|pt|Ookuninushi|ru|Окунинуси|simple|Ōkuninushi|sr|Okuninuši|sv|Ōkuninushi|tr|Ōkuninushi|uk|Окунінуші|vi|Ōkuninushi|zh|大國主|qid=Q276944|lt=Ōkuninushi-no-Mikoto}} but a different water deity to ward off water-related disasters. The current name is thought to derive from “Nagisahama / Suhama” (meaning shoreline or waterside). Incidentally, the place name “Suhama” is the oldest known place name in Daitō City.

== Shrine grounds ==

In front of the shrine buildings stands a large naturally growing kurogane-mochi tree, designated as a protected tree by Daitō City.

There are a total of eleven stone lanterns on the grounds. Among them, the lantern placed at the entrance, made in 1830 (Bunsei 13), also served as a guidepost and was relocated from the nearby {{ill|Higashi Kōya Kaidō|ja|東高野街道|qid=Q11528777}} route.
